name: Final Results from phase II of the Mainz Neutrino Mass Search in Tritium β Decay

significance.quote: We derive an upper limit of m(νe ) ≤ 2.3 eV/c2 at 95% confidence level for the mass itself.

summary.plain: The Mainz experiment's final answer: after data taking from 1997 to 2001 the electron antineutrino weighs no more than 2.3 electron-volts, at 95% confidence. It was the best direct limit of its time, shared with the Troitsk experiment.
summary.technical: Phase II final analysis of 1997-2001 tritium beta spectra: m²(νe) = (-0.6 ± 2.2 stat ± 2.1 syst) eV²/c⁴ and m(νe) ≤ 2.3 eV/c² (95% CL), ten times better signal-to-background than phase I.

title: Final Results from phase II of the Mainz Neutrino Mass Search in Tritium β Decay
why_it_matters: With Troitsk, the tightest laboratory limit on the neutrino mass for years, and the benchmark KATRIN was designed to improve by an order of magnitude.
